_why: THE SINGLE SOURCE for which client event each hook role handles.
Sprint 28, C5 audit finding F5. The role table asserted the COUNTS 6 and 4
and nothing else, so nine of the ten event names had no discriminator: rename
afterMCPExecution in the deploy, leave roles.rs alone, and both crates stay
green while the observer maps to an event Cursor never fires. That is the
ten-scripts drift the table was built to end, reproduced inside the table.
A shared constant is impossible: jawata-hook must not depend on the studio
(a hook process must never link a GUI toolkit) and the studio must not depend
on the hook (deploy writes the binary, it never runs it). Both forbidden edges
are asserted by tests. A committed data file is the one thing both sides can
read without an edge between them — each includes it at compile time and
asserts its own table against it.
Change an event here and BOTH sides fail until they agree.

_absent.cursor.recall: Cursor fires no before-a-tool-call event; afterMCPExecution is the only tool-shaped hook and it runs too late to recall INTO the call
_absent.cursor.stop: Cursor has no agent-stop event, so the stop gate cannot exist there; the discipline it enforces is carried by the rule block instead
